clue.text: Manage to perform baker's task without expression of disgust

parts.note: to make is to perform or carry out

indicators.note: without tells us to leave out the cry of disgust from the baker's phrase

parts.note: a baker's job is working dough
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get through the baking without pulling a face.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove UGH from MAKE DOUGH and MAKE DO is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is an idiom for coping or getting by with what you have.

clue.text: He pinches girl's bottom in Room At The Top and it's sporting?

indicators.note: in puts the pinching group inside the room at the top

parts.note: a room at the top of a house is an attic (also the title of a novel and film)

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip, so he holds the girl's last letter between its letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about bottom-pinching in the novel Room at the Top, presented as a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Room at the Top is John Braine's novel of a social climber, which makes the surface plausible; the girl's bottom is her last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic and sporting are synonyms describing someone fit and fond of games.

clue.text: Hates things where time is wasted for minutes

indicators.note: the time letter is thrown away and the minutes letter used in its place

parts.note: entities are things that exist

explanation.surface: A grumble about pastimes where time gets frittered away by the minute.
explanation.walkthrough: The first T of ENTITIES becomes M.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmities are hostilities or hatreds, so the plural noun matches hates used as a noun.

clue.text: Performing's first way to enjoy comedian being offensive

indicators.note: first places the performing word at the front of the rest

parts.note: a performer on stage is on

indicators.note: to enjoy something is to have it, so the way holds the comedian

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a comedian is a laugh, an entertaining character

explanation.surface: Advice for comics: perform first, the way to enjoy a comedian, even an offensive one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective about the comedian but is the noun for a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a military attack, and an onslaught is a fierce assault.

clue.text: Swearing 19 Downs are members of ENSA by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the entertainers' word is said aloud, giving the soldiers' word

parts.note: ENSA was the Entertainments National Service Association, which put on shows for British forces in World War II; its performers were troupers

explanation.surface: Foul-mouthed soldiers turn out to be the wartime entertainers, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 Down is SOLDIER; the idiom 'swear like a trooper' explains 'swearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Troopers are cavalry soldiers, proverbially foul-mouthed in the saying about swearing.

clue.text: Turnover initially higher with a salesman supported by creative form of direct marketing

indicators.note: in a down answer the creative word sits underneath the rest
initially picks the opening letter of turnover

parts.note: upper means higher
a rep is a sales representative
arty means artistic or creative

explanation.surface: Business jargon: turnover rises when a salesperson is backed by inventive direct selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic food boxes were famously sold at home gatherings hosted by a seller, a classic direct-sales method.

clue.text: Run out of Revels — they get eaten by the dozen

definitions.text: they get eaten by the dozen

indicators.note: out of tells us the run letter leaves the word for revels

parts.note: to royster (roister) is to revel noisily
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A party has run out of Revels chocolates, eaten by the dozen.
explanation.walkthrough: Revels are a British brand of mixed chocolates, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: These shellfish are traditionally bought and eaten in dozens or half-dozens.

clue.text: On time about to be captured by aliens and the like

indicators.note: on means the time word is added on after the rest
being captured means being held inside the aliens

parts.note: ET is the film alien; two of them give ET twice
C is short for circa, about
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something punctual is about to be seized by aliens and similar creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes between two ETs, and ERA is added on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, often shortened to etc., means and so on or and the rest.

clue.text: Unexpected costs hit northern folk

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters turning out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Surprise bills land on people living in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Scotland, Britain's northernmost nation, are collectively called this.

clue.text: Unpleasant smell in empty tub associated with swill, okay?

indicators.note: associated with joins the next piece on after
in puts the smell inside the emptied tub
an empty word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: hum is slang for a bad smell
to sup is to drink, to swill

explanation.surface: A smelly tub of pig swill, and someone asks if it is all right.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised-thumb gesture signals approval, meaning all is well.

clue.text: Loony South Korean dancer taps alongside duck

parts.note: Psy is the South Korean performer of Gangnam Style, known for its dance
taps are marked C and H, cold and hot
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, O

explanation.surface: A mad Korean pop star dances alongside a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Loony and the answer are both informal words for a mad person.

clue.text: How one might see TT that could set a precedent

parts.note: the two letters are the outside, the casing, of the four-letter word for a trial

explanation.surface: A question about watching the TT motorcycle races, which might set a precedent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How one might see' introduces a reverse clue: TT is how the outer letters of TEST look, so TEST CASE describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action whose ruling guides later similar disputes is so called.

clue.text: Work for Snow White's companions?

parts.note: Snow White had seven dwarfs, so a musical piece for seven performers would suit them

explanation.surface: Asking what job the seven dwarfs might do, beyond mining.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for seven players or singers is named for the number seven.

clue.text: WAGs eyed foul obliquely

indicators.note: foul suggests the letters fouled up into a new order

explanation.surface: Footballers' partners looked askance at a foul on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs are the wives and girlfriends of footballers, a British tabloid term.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways on, not head first, is moving at an angle, obliquely.

clue.text: Gouty drunk departs wanting rum — impetuous individual

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the departs letter is missing
rum means odd, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A gouty drinker leaves because there is no rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from GOUTY DRUNK and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally reformist rebels in Turkey, the phrase now means a hot-headed radical.

clue.text: Does narcotism strike only odd characters?

indicators.note: striking out the odd letters keeps the alternate even ones

explanation.surface: A question whether drug-taking affects only strange people.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts and does are synonyms in the sense of performs or behaves.

clue.text: More or less making a case for fifties affecting everyone

indicators.note: making a case means surrounding, so the approximation encloses the fifties

parts.note: around means approximately, more or less
L is the Roman numeral 50, so two make LL

explanation.surface: Arguing in favour of the 1950s because they touched everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something across the board, comprehensive, applies to all.

clue.text: What precedes twos and follows child in France is frightful

definitions.meaning: the phrase for a toddler's difficult stage around age two
the French phrase enfant ___ describes an unruly or shocking young person

explanation.surface: A riddle about what comes before twos and after a French child.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful and dreadful are synonyms for awful.

clue.text: Belt or hit cutting side of mouth

indicators.note: cutting means removing the letter from the word for hit

parts.note: to smash is to hit hard

indicators.note: a side of a word is one end, here its first letter

explanation.surface: A boxer is told to punch or strike the side of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist, a kind of belt.

clue.text: Have a stab at steps to tango first

indicators.note: first puts the tango letter before the word to

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer attempts steps, tango first.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack with a slim dagger is a verb sense, so it means to stab someone.

clue.text: Alas one's unfortunately not always available

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters going wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament that something is sadly not always on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce found only at certain times of year is available just for part of it.

clue.text: Singer and song that could blind one to reality

definitions.meaning: Alvin of that surname was a British glam-rock singer
the title of Hoagy Carmichael's standard

definitions.text: that could blind one to reality
definitions.meaning: glittering illusions in the eyes make one starry-eyed

explanation.surface: A performer and their number dazzle the audience away from reality.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic illusions are said to be magical dust in the eyes, blinding the dreamer.

clue.text: Identity reflected in more reliable fighter

indicators.note: reflected means the identity letters are turned round where they stand

parts.note: solider means sturdier, more dependable
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A self-image mirrored in a stronger warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected' reverses only the identity letters, leaving them in place within the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a member of an army, someone who fights.

clue.text: Seldom far from burnt ludicrously after vacation

parts.note: rare meat is barely cooked, far from burnt

indicators.note: after the word is vacated only its outer letters remain, following the meat word

explanation.surface: Rarely has something been so absurdly far from burnt once the holiday is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom and the answer are synonyms meaning not often.

clue.text: Fighting dog — essentially wild — is male

parts.note: a pug is a breed of small dog

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A fighting dog that is basically wild is male.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing with fists is fighting; the word comes from Latin for boxer.

clue.text: Heading off from area in north-west part of Italy

indicators.note: heading off means removing the first letter

parts.note: Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District

explanation.surface: Setting off from the north-west for somewhere in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a landlocked region of central Italy, home to Perugia and Assisi.

clue.text: Stirring up resistance in advance of eviction

indicators.note: in advance of puts the resistance letter in front

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
ousting is turning someone out, eviction

explanation.surface: Tenants stir up opposition ahead of being evicted.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or drive out, so the participle means disturbing, stirring up.

clue.text: Depressingly sad conclusion: one in 20 having ecstasy earlier

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter
in puts the one letter inside the rearranged answer to 20
earlier means the ecstasy letter is moved nearer the front

parts.note: the answer to 20 Across, meaning seldom
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gloomy ending: one in twenty takes ecstasy first.
explanation.walkthrough: RARELY with its E brought forward is REARLY; I goes in to make REARILY, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe doing something in a gloomy, dispiriting manner.

clue.text: Clever dicks wanting 50% of wage rises

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the half of wage is taken out

parts.note: know-alls are smart alecks, clever dicks

indicators.note: half of the word, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Smart alecks missing out on half their pay rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rounded hills are rises in the ground.
